exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: Strong smoothie-bar work explains every ratio and rate — here is how one student described a lemonade stand.

traits.trait: Names the ratio in words and numbers
traits.sample: My lemonade uses a 2:5 ratio — 2 cups of lemon juice for every 5 cups of water — so every batch tastes the same.
traits.why: It states the ratio both ways and says what each number counts.

traits.trait: Uses the unit rate to make a decision
traits.sample: One cup costs me $0.40 to make. Since the fair sells drinks for $1.50, my price of $1.25 undercuts them and still earns profit.
traits.why: The unit rate is computed and then actually used to justify a choice.

traits.sample: My table shows 1 batch = 7 cups, 2 batches = 14 cups, 4 batches = 28 cups, so for the class picnic I need 4 batches.
traits.why: Equivalent ratios are extended to solve a real quantity question.

traits.sample: $0.40 per cup seemed low, so I re-added my ingredient costs and got the same total — my rate checks out.
traits.why: Top work verifies the math instead of just reporting it.
